$note: Historical cook-off / bake-off results, transcribed from before the app existed, for prefilling the database once accounts/challenges can be created.
Maps onto the domain model in docs/cookingChallenge/domain-model.puml: each entry below becomes one Challenge (aggregate root: id, date, title, dishName, cookAssignments A/B, status, createdBy).

Per-category scores (Mundgefuehl/Tellersprache/Geschmack, 0-5 per dish label) are NOT known for these historical events, so no ScoreSubmission data is included -- only the already-known overall winner per challenge.

Because there are no ScoreSubmissions to run through ResultCalculator, these challenges can't be 'revealed' the normal way when imported. The importer should set status=REVEALED and 'winnerName' directly, and feed the same winner into CookRivalry.recordResult() to seed the running head-to-head record, bypassing the score-based computation.

'organizer' is the admin account (SystemRole.ADMIN) -- becomes createdBy (AccountId) on every Challenge below once accounts exist. cookA/cookB/winnerName are given as plain names here since no AccountIds exist yet; the importer must resolve/create matching Accounts first.
cookA/cookB order is arbitrary (blind labels A/B carry no meaning after the fact) -- winnerName is one of cookA/cookB, or null for a draw.
'type' distinguishes cook-off (savory) vs bake-off (dessert) events -- both use the same Challenge model, this is just a descriptive label, not a domain-model field.
Cook-off #1 date was given as '15.12.203' (typo, one digit short) -- confirmed with the user as 2023-12-15.
Cook-off #6 (Lasagne, 2026-01-17) and Bake-off #1 (Apfelkuchen, 2026-01-17) share the same date -- confirmed as two distinct events on the same day, not a data error.
Entries are kept in the order/numbering given by the user, which is not strictly chronological (#5 2026-04-11 precedes #6 2026-01-17 in the list).
